text:
«Once, if I remember correctly, my life was a feast where every heart opened, where every wine flowed.


One night, I sat Beauty on my knees. —And I found her bitter.— And I insulted her.


I armed myself against justice.


And I fled. Oh witches, oh misery, oh hatred; only to you was my treasure entrusted!


I managed to banish every human hope from my mind. Over every joy, to strangle it, I carried out the muffled assault of the savage beast.


I called the executioners so I could die biting the butt of their rifles. I invoked plagues to suffocate me with sand, with blood. Misfortune was my god. I hurled myself against the mud. The air of crime dried me out. I played tricks on madness.


And spring gave me the frightful laughter of the idiot.


But now, recently, when I was about to breathe my last, I thought of seeking the key to the old feast, at which, perhaps, I would regain my appetite.


Charity is that key. —That inspired assertion proves that I have been dreaming!


«You will remain a hyena, etc…» declares the demon who crowned me with such pleasant poppies. «Earn your death with all your appetites, and with your selfishness and all the deadly sins».


Ah! I have endured enough: —But, dear Satan, I beg you, do not be so angry with me! And while I await those little vile acts I still have left to commit, I detach for you, who love in the writer the absence of every descriptive or instructive faculty, a few disgusting pages from my notebook of the condemned.




A Season in Hell, 1873

translation.title: Once, If I Remember Correctly
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the stored Spanish rendering, not from Rimbaud's French original. The stray line break before the comma in the source's closing publication line is repaired; the translation preserves the quoted voices, reversals, and grotesque imagery.
